meta.title: Muscles worked by daily life
meta.scope: Every muscle in muscles.json, rated by how much an ordinary day without exercise works it, with the everyday activities that do.
meta.baseline: An ordinary day for a healthy adult who does no exercise: sleep, washing and dressing, meals, conversation, sitting at a desk or table, a few thousand steps, a few flights of stairs, getting in and out of chairs, bed and a car, carrying bags, light chores, phone and keyboard use, and trips to the toilet.
conventions: One entry per muscles.json entry, in the same order; 'id' and 'name' match muscles.json.
'tier' is a key of meta.tiers. 'activities' lists keys of meta.activities, most important first; it is empty when nothing in an ordinary day works the muscle.
Muscles not everyone has ('variable' in muscles.json) are rated for the people who have them.
Tiers say how often daily life works a muscle, not how hard. Most everyday use of the limb and trunk muscles is light.
Ratings are qualitative, from each muscle's known actions and, where studied, its activity in everyday movement. They are not measurements.

tiers.nonstop: Works around the clock, or every waking moment, with no effort from you: the heartbeat, breathing, eye movements and blinking, the airway, digestion, and the tone that keeps the bladder and bowel closed.
tiers.daily: Works many times a day, or for long stretches, in things everyone does: sitting and standing, walking, getting up, eating, talking, facial expression, holding up and turning the head, using the hands.
tiers.occasional: Works only in some situations, not every day for everyone: cold, arousal, deep labored breathing.
tiers.barely: Vestigial, or no clear everyday action: little or no work in an ordinary day.

activities.heartbeat: Heartbeat: The heart's own rhythm, about 100,000 beats a day.
activities.breathing: Breathing: Quiet breathing, roughly 20,000 breaths a day, plus sighs, yawns and harder breathing on stairs.
activities.looking: Looking & blinking: Eye movements, focusing, pupil changes, blinking and holding the eyes open.
activities.expression: Facial expression: Smiling, frowning, raising the eyebrows, squinting.
activities.eating: Eating & swallowing: Biting, chewing, sipping and swallowing food, drink and saliva.
activities.digestion: Digestion: Moving food, bile and pancreatic juice along the gut, without any effort from you.
activities.continence: Bladder & bowel: Holding urine and stool around the clock, and emptying the bladder and bowel.
activities.head: Holding & turning the head: Keeping the head up while you sit or stand, looking around, nodding.
activities.upright: Sitting & standing: Holding the trunk upright and balancing on your feet.
activities.walking: Walking: Everyday walking on level ground.
activities.stairs: Stairs & slopes: Climbing and descending stairs, curbs and hills.
activities.rising: Getting up & down: Getting into and out of chairs, bed, the toilet and a car; sitting up in bed.
activities.bending: Bending & picking up: Bending over to pick things up, load a dishwasher or tie your shoes.
activities.carrying: Lifting & carrying: Bags, groceries, laundry, children, boxes.
activities.reaching: Reaching & dressing: Reaching forward and overhead, dressing, washing and brushing your hair.
activities.pushing: Pushing & pulling: Doors, drawers, carts, a vacuum cleaner.
activities.gripping: Gripping: Holding a phone, cup, bag or rail; opening jars; turning keys and doorknobs.
activities.fine: Fine hand work: Typing, writing, tapping a phone, doing up buttons, using cutlery.
activities.forced: Coughing & straining: Forced breathing out and bearing down: coughs, sneezes, laughs, straining on the toilet, bracing for a lift.
activities.reflexes: Reflexes: Automatic responses to cold, touch, loud sound or a startle.
activities.sexual: Sexual function: Erection, arousal and ejaculation.

muscles.name: Levator palpebrae superioris
muscles.note: Holds the upper eyelid open every waking moment; relaxes for each blink and in sleep.

muscles.name: Superior rectus
muscles.note: Turns the eye up. The eye muscles work in every glance, about three quick jumps (saccades) a second while awake, and in REM sleep.

muscles.name: Inferior rectus
muscles.note: Turns the eye down, as when reading or looking at a phone.

muscles.name: Medial rectus
muscles.note: Turns the eye inward; the two work together to converge on anything close, like a screen or a page.

muscles.name: Lateral rectus
muscles.note: Turns the eye outward, as when glancing to the side.

muscles.name: Superior oblique
muscles.note: Turns the eye down and in and rotates it; needed for looking down while reading or going downstairs.

muscles.name: Inferior oblique
muscles.note: Turns the eye up and out and rotates it, keeping the view level when you tilt your head.

muscles.name: Tensor tympani
muscles.note: Tightens the eardrum when you chew, swallow and yawn, and in a startle.

muscles.name: Stapedius
muscles.note: Damps the smallest ear bone just before and while you speak, and reflexively to loud sounds.

muscles.name: Occipitofrontalis
muscles.note: The frontal belly raises the eyebrows in surprise and when looking up; the occipital belly anchors the scalp.

muscles.name: Temporoparietalis
muscles.note: Thin, largely vestigial scalp sheet; little role in an ordinary day.

muscles.name: Orbicularis oculi
muscles.note: Closes the lids for every blink (about 15,000 a day), squints against glare and crinkles the eyes in a smile; its deep part helps drain tears.

muscles.name: Corrugator supercilii
muscles.note: Draws the brows together to frown, concentrate or squint against glare.

muscles.name: Depressor supercilii
muscles.note: Pulls the brow down when frowning or shading the eyes from light.

muscles.name: Procerus
muscles.note: Pulls the skin between the brows down, wrinkling the bridge of the nose in a frown or squint.

muscles.name: Nasalis
muscles.note: Flares the nostrils when you sniff or breathe hard, and compresses them.

muscles.name: Depressor septi nasi
muscles.note: Pulls the tip of the nose down when you smile or talk and helps widen the nostrils on a deep breath.

muscles.name: Orbicularis oris
muscles.note: Closes and purses the lips for speech (p, b, m, w), sipping and keeping food and drink in the mouth.

muscles.name: Buccinator
muscles.note: Holds the cheeks against the teeth to keep food between them while chewing; also used to suck and blow.

muscles.name: Levator labii superioris
muscles.note: Raises the upper lip in a broad smile, a sneer or speech.

muscles.name: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
muscles.note: Lifts the upper lip and flares the nostril, as in a sneer or a broad smile.

muscles.name: Levator anguli oris
muscles.note: Lifts the corners of the mouth in a smile.

muscles.name: Zygomaticus major
muscles.note: The main smiling muscle: draws the corners of the mouth up and out.

muscles.name: Zygomaticus minor
muscles.note: Lifts the upper lip to show the upper teeth when smiling.

muscles.name: Risorius
muscles.note: Where present, pulls the corners of the mouth sideways in a grin.

muscles.name: Depressor anguli oris
muscles.note: Pulls the corners of the mouth down, as in a frown or grimace.

muscles.name: Transversus menti
muscles.note: Where present, works with depressor anguli oris.

muscles.name: Depressor labii inferioris
muscles.note: Lowers the lower lip in speech, pouting and showing the lower teeth.

muscles.name: Mentalis
muscles.note: Raises and pushes out the lower lip, as in pouting or sealing the lip against a cup, and wrinkles the chin.

muscles.name: Anterior auricular
muscles.note: Vestigial; pulls the ear forward only in people who can wiggle their ears.

muscles.name: Superior auricular
muscles.note: Vestigial; lifts the ear only in people who can wiggle their ears.

muscles.name: Posterior auricular
muscles.note: Vestigial; twitches reflexively to sudden sounds, too little to move the ear in most people.

muscles.name: Helicis major
muscles.note: Vestigial ear-shape muscle; no useful action in humans.

muscles.name: Helicis minor
muscles.note: Vestigial ear-shape muscle; no useful action in humans.

muscles.name: Tragicus
muscles.note: Vestigial ear-shape muscle; no useful action in humans.

muscles.name: Pyramidal muscle of auricle
muscles.note: Vestigial ear-shape muscle; no useful action in humans.

muscles.name: Antitragicus
muscles.note: Vestigial ear-shape muscle; no useful action in humans.

muscles.name: Transverse muscle of auricle
muscles.note: Vestigial ear-shape muscle; no useful action in humans.

muscles.name: Oblique muscle of auricle
muscles.note: Vestigial ear-shape muscle; no useful action in humans.

muscles.name: Muscle of terminal notch
muscles.note: Vestigial ear-shape muscle; no useful action in humans.

muscles.name: Masseter
muscles.note: The main chewing muscle: closes the jaw to bite and chew, and clenches the teeth.

muscles.name: Temporalis
muscles.note: Closes and pulls back the jaw in chewing, and helps hold it closed at rest.

muscles.name: Lateral pterygoid
muscles.note: Opens the jaw and moves it forward and side to side, in chewing, talking and yawning.

muscles.name: Medial pterygoid
muscles.note: Closes the jaw with the masseter and grinds food side to side.

muscles.name: Pterygoideus proprius
muscles.note: Where present, works with the lateral pterygoid.

muscles.name: Genioglossus
muscles.note: Pushes the tongue forward; its activity with each breath keeps the airway open, awake and asleep, and it shapes every swallow and word.

muscles.name: Hyoglossus
muscles.note: Pulls the sides of the tongue down in chewing, swallowing and speech.

muscles.name: Chondroglossus
muscles.note: Part of hyoglossus; works with it.

muscles.name: Triticeoglossus
muscles.note: Where present, pulls the tongue back and down with hyoglossus.

muscles.name: Styloglossus
muscles.note: Pulls the tongue up and back to start each swallow and to make sounds like k and g.

muscles.name: Palatoglossus
muscles.note: Raises the back of the tongue and narrows the entrance to the throat in swallowing.

muscles.name: Superior longitudinal muscle of tongue
muscles.note: Curls the tongue tip up for sounds like t, d and l, and moves food around the mouth.

muscles.name: Inferior longitudinal muscle of tongue
muscles.note: Curls the tongue tip down in speech and swallowing.

muscles.name: Transverse muscle of tongue
muscles.note: Narrows and lengthens the tongue, as for s sounds or sticking it out.

muscles.name: Vertical muscle of tongue
muscles.note: Flattens and widens the tongue in chewing and speech.

muscles.name: Levator veli palatini
muscles.note: Lifts the soft palate to seal off the nose in every swallow and most speech sounds.

muscles.name: Tensor veli palatini
muscles.note: Tenses the soft palate and opens the Eustachian tube when you swallow or yawn, equalizing ear pressure.

muscles.name: Musculus uvulae
muscles.note: Shortens and thickens the uvula to help seal off the nose.

muscles.name: Palatopharyngeus
muscles.note: Raises the throat and closes off the nasal passage during swallowing.

muscles.name: Platysma
muscles.note: Tenses the skin of the neck and pulls the mouth corners down in a grimace or when bracing.

muscles.name: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.note: Turns and tilts the head and lifts it off the pillow; lifts the breastbone in hard breathing.

muscles.name: Digastric
muscles.note: Opens the jaw, hardest in a yawn, and raises the hyoid bone in each swallow.

muscles.name: Stylohyoid
muscles.note: Pulls the hyoid bone up and back when you swallow.

muscles.name: Mylohyoid
muscles.note: Raises the floor of the mouth, pushing the tongue up in each swallow.

muscles.name: Geniohyoid
muscles.note: Pulls the hyoid bone forward in swallowing, widening the throat, and helps open the jaw.

muscles.name: Sternohyoid
muscles.note: Pulls the hyoid bone back down after each swallow and steadies it in speech.

muscles.name: Omohyoid
muscles.note: Pulls the hyoid bone down after swallowing and steadies it in speech.

muscles.name: Sternothyroid
muscles.note: Pulls the larynx down after swallowing and for low notes.

muscles.name: Thyrohyoid
muscles.note: Raises the larynx toward the hyoid bone in swallowing and speech.

muscles.name: Levator glandulae thyroideae
muscles.note: Inconstant band on the thyroid gland; no clear action.

muscles.name: Longus colli
muscles.note: Steadies the curve of the neck and bends it forward; works whenever you hold the head up or nod.

muscles.name: Longus capitis
muscles.note: Nods the head forward and steadies it on the neck.

muscles.name: Rectus capitis anterior
muscles.note: Nods the head at the skull joint and steadies it.

muscles.name: Rectus capitis lateralis
muscles.note: Tilts the head sideways and steadies it on the top vertebra.

muscles.name: Anterior scalene
muscles.note: Lifts the first rib with every breath, quiet ones included, and bends the neck sideways.

muscles.name: Middle scalene
muscles.note: Lifts the first rib with every breath and bends the neck sideways.

muscles.name: Posterior scalene
muscles.note: Lifts the second rib with every breath and bends the neck sideways.

muscles.name: Scalenus minimus
muscles.note: Where present, tightens the membrane over the top of the lung; no clear everyday action.

muscles.name: Rectus capitis posterior major
muscles.note: Tips the head back and turns it; fine-tunes head position as the eyes move.

muscles.name: Rectus capitis posterior minor
muscles.note: Tips the head back and steadies it; unusually rich in stretch sensors that track head position.

muscles.name: Obliquus capitis superior
muscles.note: Tips the head back and sideways in small posture adjustments.

muscles.name: Obliquus capitis inferior
muscles.note: Turns the head at the top two vertebrae, as in looking over your shoulder.

muscles.name: Superior pharyngeal constrictor
muscles.note: Squeezes food, drink and saliva down the throat in each swallow, several hundred times a day.

muscles.name: Middle pharyngeal constrictor
muscles.note: Squeezes each swallow down the throat.

muscles.name: Inferior pharyngeal constrictor
muscles.note: Squeezes each swallow down; its lowest part (cricopharyngeus) stays clenched day and night as the upper esophageal sphincter, opening only to let a swallow through.

muscles.name: Stylopharyngeus
muscles.note: Lifts and widens the throat to take each swallow.

muscles.name: Salpingopharyngeus
muscles.note: Raises the throat in swallowing and helps open the Eustachian tube.

muscles.name: Cricothyroid
muscles.note: Stretches the vocal folds to raise the pitch of the voice.

muscles.name: Posterior cricoarytenoid
muscles.note: The only muscle that opens the vocal folds; widens them a little with every breath in, awake and asleep.

muscles.name: Ceratocricoid
muscles.note: Inconstant slip beside the posterior cricoarytenoid; its action, if any, is unclear.

muscles.name: Lateral cricoarytenoid
muscles.note: Closes the vocal folds to make voice, and to hold the breath before a cough or a lift.

muscles.name: Thyroarytenoid
muscles.note: Shortens and closes the vocal folds for speech, and seals the airway in swallowing and coughing.

muscles.name: Vocalis
muscles.note: Fine-tunes the tension of the vocal folds for pitch and voice quality.

muscles.name: Oblique arytenoid
muscles.note: Closes the entrance to the larynx in each swallow and helps close the vocal folds.

muscles.name: Transverse arytenoid
muscles.note: Closes the back of the vocal folds for voice and in swallowing.

muscles.name: Trapezius
muscles.note: The upper part holds up the shoulders against the weight of the arms and anything carried; the whole muscle turns the shoulder blade up when you reach overhead.

muscles.name: Latissimus dorsi
muscles.note: Pulls the arm down and back: pushing up from armrests or a bed, pulling a door, reaching into a back pocket; also squeezes the chest in a hard cough.

muscles.name: Rhomboid major
muscles.note: Pulls the shoulder blade back and steadies it when you pull, carry or reach.

muscles.name: Rhomboid minor
muscles.note: Pulls the shoulder blade back and steadies it, with the major.

muscles.name: Levator scapulae
muscles.note: Lifts the shoulder blade and bends the neck; works in shrugging, carrying and holding the head forward over a screen.

muscles.name: Transversus nuchae
muscles.note: Inconstant slip over the top of the back of the neck; no clear action.

muscles.name: Serratus posterior superior
muscles.note: Textbooks say it lifts the upper ribs in deep breaths; direct evidence for any breathing role is thin.

muscles.name: Serratus posterior inferior
muscles.note: Textbooks say it holds down the lower ribs in deep breaths; direct evidence for any breathing role is thin.

muscles.name: Splenius capitis
muscles.note: Holds the head up and turns it to the same side; works harder with the head forward over a phone or desk.

muscles.name: Splenius cervicis
muscles.note: Holds the neck extended and turns it.

muscles.name: Iliocostalis lumborum
muscles.note: Holds the lower back upright, lowers and raises the trunk when you bend, and braces it when you lift.

muscles.name: Iliocostalis thoracis
muscles.note: Holds the mid back upright and helps bend it sideways.

muscles.name: Iliocostalis cervicis
muscles.note: Holds the lower neck extended.

muscles.name: Longissimus thoracis
muscles.note: The longest back extensor: keeps the trunk upright and controls every bend and lift.

muscles.name: Longissimus cervicis
muscles.note: Holds the neck extended and bends it sideways.

muscles.name: Longissimus capitis
muscles.note: Holds the head up and tips it back or to the side.

muscles.name: Spinalis thoracis
muscles.note: Holds the mid back extended.

muscles.name: Spinalis cervicis
muscles.note: Where present, holds the neck extended.

muscles.name: Spinalis capitis
muscles.note: Holds the head up, blended with semispinalis capitis.

muscles.name: Semispinalis thoracis
muscles.note: Holds the upper back extended and turns it slightly.

muscles.name: Semispinalis cervicis
muscles.note: Holds the neck extended; a key deep stabilizer of the neck.

muscles.name: Semispinalis capitis
muscles.note: The main muscle holding the head up: works whenever you sit or stand, and harder when you look down.

muscles.name: Multifidus
muscles.note: Stiffens each spinal segment: switches on just before you move an arm or leg, and works in every step, bend and lift.

muscles.name: Rotatores lumborum
muscles.note: Short segmental muscles packed with stretch sensors; steady and sense each vertebra in posture and twisting.

muscles.name: Rotatores thoracis
muscles.note: Short segmental muscles packed with stretch sensors; steady and sense each vertebra in posture and twisting.

muscles.name: Rotatores cervicis
muscles.note: Short segmental muscles that steady and sense the neck vertebrae.

muscles.name: Interspinales cervicis
muscles.note: Short muscles between the spines of the neck vertebrae; steady the neck as it straightens.

muscles.name: Interspinales thoracis
muscles.note: Short muscles between vertebral spines; steady the spine as it straightens.

muscles.name: Interspinales lumborum
muscles.note: Short muscles between vertebral spines; steady the lower back as it straightens.

muscles.name: Anterior cervical intertransversarii
muscles.note: Short muscles between the side processes of the neck vertebrae; steady side bending and sense position.

muscles.name: Lateral posterior cervical intertransversarii
muscles.note: Short muscles between the side processes of the neck vertebrae; steady side bending and sense position.

muscles.name: Medial posterior cervical intertransversarii
muscles.note: Short muscles between the side processes of the neck vertebrae; steady side bending and sense position.

muscles.name: Thoracic intertransversarii
muscles.note: Short muscles between the side processes; steady the spine in side bending.

muscles.name: Lateral lumbar intertransversarii
muscles.note: Short muscles between the side processes of the lumbar vertebrae; steady side bending.

muscles.name: Medial lumbar intertransversarii
muscles.note: Short muscles between the lumbar vertebrae; steady and sense segment position.

muscles.name: Pectoralis major
muscles.note: Brings the arm forward and across: pushing doors, carrying things in front of you, hugging, pushing up from a chair.

muscles.name: Pectoralis minor
muscles.note: Draws the shoulder blade forward and down when you reach or push; helps lift the ribs in deep breaths.

muscles.name: Subclavius
muscles.note: Steadies the collarbone against the breastbone as the arm moves.

muscles.name: Serratus anterior
muscles.note: Holds the shoulder blade to the ribs and turns it up when you reach forward or overhead or push.

muscles.name: Sternalis
muscles.note: Present in a small minority; no known action.

muscles.name: External intercostals
muscles.note: Lift the ribs with every breath in and keep the chest wall firm.

muscles.name: Internal intercostals
muscles.note: The front parts help lift the ribs with every breath in; the side parts pull the ribs down in speech, coughing and forced breathing out.

muscles.name: Innermost intercostals
muscles.note: Work with the internal intercostals, pulling the ribs down in speech, coughs and forced breaths out.

muscles.name: Subcostales
muscles.note: Thought to pull the lower ribs down with the internal intercostals.

muscles.name: Transversus thoracis
muscles.note: Pulls the front of the ribs down when breathing out takes effort: speaking, coughing, laughing.

muscles.name: Levatores costarum
muscles.note: Lift the ribs when you breathe in and help bend and turn the spine.

muscles.name: Diaphragm
muscles.note: The main breathing muscle: contracts with every breath, roughly 20,000 a day, awake and asleep. Also pushes down to cough, sneeze, strain on the toilet and brace for a lift.

muscles.name: Rectus abdominis
muscles.note: Curls the trunk to sit up in bed or from a sofa, and squeezes the belly in coughs, laughs and straining.

muscles.name: Pyramidalis
muscles.note: Where present, tenses the midline of the belly wall; no clear everyday role.

muscles.name: External oblique
muscles.note: Turns and side-bends the trunk, steadies it when you reach or carry, and squeezes the belly to cough, laugh or strain.

muscles.name: Internal oblique
muscles.note: Turns and side-bends the trunk with the external oblique; its lower fibers stay lightly active while you stand.

muscles.name: Transversus abdominis
muscles.note: Tightens the belly like a corset: switches on just before you move a limb, and in coughs, laughs, lifts and bearing down on the toilet.

muscles.name: Cremaster
muscles.note: Lifts the testis in cold, when the inner thigh is touched (the cremasteric reflex) and in arousal; in females only a few fibers.

muscles.name: Quadratus lumborum
muscles.note: Hikes the hip and holds the trunk level when you walk or carry a bag in one hand; anchors the lowest rib for breathing.

muscles.name: Pubococcygeus
muscles.note: Levator ani keeps a steady tone all day to hold up the pelvic organs, and clenches reflexively when you cough, sneeze, laugh or lift.

muscles.name: Puboperinealis
muscles.note: Part of levator ani; supports the perineal body with the rest of the pelvic floor.

muscles.name: Pubovaginalis / Puboprostaticus
muscles.note: Part of levator ani; supports the vagina or prostate and helps close the urethra.

muscles.name: Puboanalis
muscles.note: Part of levator ani; supports the anal canal.

muscles.name: Puborectalis
muscles.note: Sling around the rectum that stays contracted to keep the bowel closed; relaxes only when you empty it.

muscles.name: Iliococcygeus
muscles.note: Part of levator ani; forms the back of the pelvic floor and holds up the pelvic organs.

muscles.name: Coccygeus
muscles.note: Supports the back of the pelvic floor and pulls the tailbone forward again after a bowel movement.

muscles.name: External anal sphincter
muscles.note: Keeps a steady clench day and night, tightens when you cough or hold in gas, and relaxes to let you empty the bowel.

muscles.name: Superficial transverse perineal
muscles.note: Steadies the perineal body, the pelvic floor's central anchor, when you cough, lift or strain.

muscles.name: Ischiocavernosus
muscles.note: Stiffens the erect penis or clitoris; works mainly in sexual activity.

muscles.name: Bulbospongiosus
muscles.note: In males, clears the last urine from the urethra after each void and expels semen; in females, narrows the vaginal opening.

muscles.name: Deep transverse perineal
muscles.note: Steadies the perineal body and supports the urethral sphincter.

muscles.name: External urethral sphincter
muscles.note: Keeps the urethra closed around the clock and squeezes harder when you cough, laugh or need to hold on; relaxes to let you urinate.

muscles.name: Compressor urethrae
muscles.note: Female; part of the urethral sphincter complex that keeps the urethra closed.

muscles.name: Sphincter urethrovaginalis
muscles.note: Female; wraps the urethra and vagina and helps keep the urethra closed.

muscles.name: Deltoid
muscles.note: Lifts the arm in every direction: reaching for a shelf, washing your hair, holding a bag away from the body.

muscles.name: Supraspinatus
muscles.note: Starts every arm raise and keeps the shoulder joint seated, even while a bag hangs from your hand.

muscles.name: Infraspinatus
muscles.note: Turns the arm out and steadies the shoulder: brushing your hair, reaching to the side.

muscles.name: Teres minor
muscles.note: Turns the arm out and steadies the shoulder with infraspinatus.

muscles.name: Subscapularis
muscles.note: Turns the arm in and guards the front of the shoulder: tucking in a shirt, reaching behind your back, pushing.

muscles.name: Teres major
muscles.note: Pulls the arm down and back with the latissimus dorsi, as in pushing up from armrests or pulling a door.

muscles.name: Biceps brachii
muscles.note: Bends the elbow and turns the palm up: bringing a fork or cup to your mouth, carrying bags on the forearm, turning a key.

muscles.name: Coracobrachialis
muscles.note: Brings the arm forward and across the body.

muscles.name: Brachialis
muscles.note: The main elbow bender whatever the palm's position; works whenever you lift something toward you.

muscles.name: Triceps brachii
muscles.note: Straightens the elbow: pushing up from a chair or bed, pushing doors and carts.

muscles.name: Anconeus
muscles.note: Helps straighten the elbow and steadies it as the forearm turns.

muscles.name: Articularis cubiti
muscles.note: Draws the elbow capsule clear each time the arm straightens.

muscles.name: Pronator teres
muscles.note: Turns the palm down, for typing or pouring, and helps bend the elbow.

muscles.name: Flexor carpi radialis
muscles.note: Bends the wrist and steadies it in grip.

muscles.name: Palmaris longus
muscles.note: Where present, tenses the palm and weakly bends the wrist in grip.

muscles.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
muscles.note: Bends the wrist toward the little finger and steadies it when you carry, hammer or type.

muscles.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis
muscles.note: Bends the fingers in every grip: bags, cups, rails, phones.

muscles.name: Flexor digitorum profundus
muscles.note: The only muscle that bends the fingertips; takes the load in hook grips such as carrying shopping bags.

muscles.name: Flexor pollicis longus
muscles.note: Bends the thumb tip for pinching, writing and texting.

muscles.name: Pronator quadratus
muscles.note: The main palm-down turner; also holds the forearm bones together when you grip or push.

muscles.name: Brachioradialis
muscles.note: Bends the elbow with the thumb up, as when lifting a mug or carrying a bag by its handle.

muscles.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus
muscles.note: Holds the wrist cocked back during grip and typing.

muscles.name: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
muscles.note: The main wrist stabilizer in grip and typing; the muscle usually behind tennis elbow.

muscles.name: Extensor digitorum
muscles.note: Straightens the fingers to let go of things, type and spread the hand.

muscles.name: Extensor digiti minimi
muscles.note: Straightens the little finger.

muscles.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris
muscles.note: Steadies the wrist in grip and bends it toward the little finger, as when steering a mouse.

muscles.name: Supinator
muscles.note: Turns the palm up: turning a doorknob or key, using a screwdriver, holding out a hand.

muscles.name: Abductor pollicis longus
muscles.note: Swings the thumb out from the palm to open the hand around objects.

muscles.name: Extensor pollicis brevis
muscles.note: Straightens the base of the thumb, in texting and in opening the hand to grip.

muscles.name: Extensor pollicis longus
muscles.note: Straightens the thumb tip and pulls it back, lifting it off a phone screen or space bar.

muscles.name: Extensor indicis
muscles.note: Straightens the index finger to point, tap a screen or click.

muscles.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
muscles.note: Moves the thumb away from the palm to wrap around a cup or phone.

muscles.name: Flexor pollicis brevis
muscles.note: Bends the thumb at its base in pinch and grip.

muscles.name: Opponens pollicis
muscles.note: Swings the thumb across the palm to meet the fingertips, the basis of every pinch and grasp.

muscles.name: Adductor pollicis
muscles.note: Presses the thumb against the hand, as in holding keys, a card or a phone.

muscles.name: Palmaris brevis
muscles.note: Wrinkles and cushions the skin at the little-finger edge of the palm to firm up a grip.

muscles.name: Abductor digiti minimi (hand)
muscles.note: Spreads the little finger for a wide grip or a reach across the keyboard.

muscles.name: Flexor digiti minimi brevis (hand)
muscles.note: Bends the little finger at its base.

muscles.name: Opponens digiti minimi (hand)
muscles.note: Cups the palm by rolling the little finger toward the thumb.

muscles.name: Lumbricals (hand)
muscles.note: Bend the knuckles while straightening the fingers: holding a card, typing, writing.

muscles.name: Dorsal interossei (hand)
muscles.note: Spread the fingers and steady them in grip and typing.

muscles.name: Palmar interossei
muscles.note: Draw the fingers together, as when holding a flat hand or a sheet of paper.

muscles.name: Pollical palmar interosseus
muscles.note: Where recognized, draws the thumb in with adductor pollicis.

muscles.name: Psoas major
muscles.note: Lifts the thigh in every step and stair and steadies the lower spine when you sit upright.

muscles.name: Psoas minor
muscles.note: Absent in many people; where present, a weak helper in bending the lower trunk with no clear everyday job.

muscles.name: Iliacus
muscles.note: Swings the leg forward in every step with psoas major and tilts the pelvis to sit upright.

muscles.name: Gluteus maximus
muscles.note: Straightens the hip to stand up, climb stairs and come up from a bend; level walking uses little of it.

muscles.name: Gluteus medius
muscles.note: Keeps the pelvis level each time a foot leaves the ground, in every step and stair.

muscles.name: Gluteus minimus
muscles.note: Keeps the pelvis level and the hip steady with gluteus medius.

muscles.name: Tensor fasciae latae
muscles.note: Steadies the hip and knee through the iliotibial band in walking and standing.

muscles.name: Piriformis
muscles.note: Turns the thigh out and steadies the hip joint in walking and standing.

muscles.name: Superior gemellus
muscles.note: Steadies the hip joint and turns the thigh out with the other deep rotators.

muscles.name: Obturator internus
muscles.note: Steadies the hip joint; part of the pelvic floor is anchored to its covering.

muscles.name: Inferior gemellus
muscles.note: Steadies the hip joint and turns the thigh out.

muscles.name: Quadratus femoris
muscles.note: Turns the thigh out and steadies the hip joint.

muscles.name: Obturator externus
muscles.note: Turns the thigh out and steadies the hip joint.

muscles.name: Sartorius
muscles.note: Bends and turns out the thigh and bends the knee: crossing your legs, stepping into a car, sitting cross-legged.

muscles.name: Rectus femoris
muscles.note: Straightens the knee and lifts the thigh: swinging each step forward, climbing stairs, standing up.

muscles.name: Vastus lateralis
muscles.note: Straightens the knee to stand up and climb, and cushions each step and each stair on the way down.

muscles.name: Vastus intermedius
muscles.note: Straightens the knee with the other vasti.

muscles.name: Vastus medialis
muscles.note: Straightens the knee and steadies the kneecap, especially as the leg straightens fully.

muscles.name: Articularis genus
muscles.note: Pulls the knee capsule up out of the way whenever the knee straightens.

muscles.name: Pectineus
muscles.note: Draws the thigh forward and in during each step.

muscles.name: Adductor longus
muscles.note: Pulls the leg in and steadies the pelvis in walking and standing.

muscles.name: Adductor brevis
muscles.note: Pulls the leg in and helps bring it forward in each step.

muscles.name: Adductor magnus
muscles.note: Its hamstring part straightens the hip to stand up and climb; its adductor part steadies the leg in each step.

muscles.name: Adductor minimus
muscles.note: Upper part of adductor magnus; works with it.

muscles.name: Gracilis
muscles.note: Pulls the leg in, helps bend the knee and steadies the inner knee in each step.

muscles.name: Biceps femoris
muscles.note: Brakes the swinging leg at the end of each step and helps straighten the hip when you rise from a bend or a chair.

muscles.name: Semitendinosus
muscles.note: Brakes the swinging leg and helps straighten the hip, like biceps femoris; also steadies the inner knee.

muscles.name: Semimembranosus
muscles.note: Brakes the leg at the end of each step and helps straighten the hip.

muscles.name: Tibialis anterior
muscles.note: Lifts the foot in every step so the toes clear the ground, lowers it gently after heel strike, and corrects your balance when standing.

muscles.name: Extensor hallucis longus
muscles.note: Lifts the big toe and helps lift the foot in each step.

muscles.name: Extensor digitorum longus
muscles.note: Lifts the toes and foot so they clear the ground in each step.

muscles.name: Fibularis tertius
muscles.note: Where present, lifts the outer edge of the foot as it swings through.

muscles.name: Fibularis longus
muscles.note: Braces the ankle against rolling over and supports the arch in every step and in standing balance.

muscles.name: Fibularis brevis
muscles.note: Braces the ankle and turns the sole outward, guarding against ankle rolls.

muscles.name: Gastrocnemius
muscles.note: Pushes off at the end of each step and lifts the heel on stairs; also bends the knee.

muscles.name: Soleus
muscles.note: Works continuously while you stand to keep you from tipping forward, pushes off in each step, and its squeeze pumps blood back up from the legs.

muscles.name: Plantaris
muscles.note: Where present, a thin helper of the calf.

muscles.name: Popliteus
muscles.note: Unlocks the straightened knee so it can bend, as when you start to sit or take a step, and steadies it.

muscles.name: Flexor hallucis longus
muscles.note: Presses the big toe down for the final push-off of each step.

muscles.name: Flexor digitorum longus
muscles.note: Curls the toes to grip the ground and helps hold up the arch.

muscles.name: Tibialis posterior
muscles.note: Holds up the inner arch in every step and in standing.

muscles.name: Extensor digitorum brevis
muscles.note: Lifts the toes with the long toe extensor.

muscles.name: Extensor hallucis brevis
muscles.note: Lifts the big toe with the long extensor.

muscles.name: Abductor hallucis
muscles.note: Supports the inner arch and steadies the big toe in standing and push-off.

muscles.name: Flexor digitorum brevis
muscles.note: Curls the toes and firms the arch as you push off and balance.

muscles.name: Abductor digiti minimi (foot)
muscles.note: Supports the outer edge of the foot in standing and walking.

muscles.name: Abductor ossis metatarsi quinti
muscles.note: Where present, helps the muscles of the outer foot.

muscles.name: Quadratus plantae
muscles.note: Straightens the pull of the long toe flexor so the toes press down evenly in push-off.

muscles.name: Lumbricals (foot)
muscles.note: Keep the toes flat and straight under load as you walk.

muscles.name: Flexor hallucis brevis
muscles.note: Presses the big toe down for push-off and balance.

muscles.name: Adductor hallucis
muscles.note: Holds the forefoot together and supports its cross arch.

muscles.name: Flexor digiti minimi brevis (foot)
muscles.note: Presses the little toe down in push-off.

muscles.name: Opponens digiti minimi (foot)
muscles.note: Where present, works with flexor digiti minimi brevis.

muscles.name: Plantar interossei
muscles.note: Hold the toes together and steady them under load.

muscles.name: Dorsal interossei (foot)
muscles.note: Spread and steady the toes as they grip the ground.

muscles.name: Levator claviculae
muscles.note: Where present, lifts the collarbone with the upper trapezius.

muscles.name: Axillary arch muscle
muscles.note: Where present, a slip of the latissimus dorsi that works with it; can press on the nerves in the armpit.

muscles.name: Chondroepitrochlearis
muscles.note: Where present, a slip of the pectoralis major that works with it.

muscles.name: Anconeus epitrochlearis
muscles.note: Where present, tightens as the elbow straightens; can press on the ulnar nerve.

muscles.name: Gantzer's muscle
muscles.note: Where present, an extra head of flexor pollicis longus that works with it.

muscles.name: Extensor digitorum brevis manus
muscles.note: Where present, helps straighten the index or middle finger.

muscles.name: Fibularis quartus
muscles.note: Where present, works with the fibularis muscles to brace the ankle.

muscles.name: Accessory soleus
muscles.note: Where present, works with the soleus in standing and walking.

muscles.name: Ciliary muscle
muscles.note: Focuses the eye: contracts for as long as you look at anything close, like a screen, book or phone, and relaxes for distance.

muscles.name: Sphincter pupillae
muscles.note: Narrows the pupil in bright light and for near vision, adjusting all day.

muscles.name: Dilator pupillae
muscles.note: Widens the pupil in dim light and with alertness or excitement.

muscles.name: Superior tarsal
muscles.note: Its steady tone lifts the upper lid an extra millimeter or two while you are awake; the lid droops when you are tired.

muscles.name: Inferior tarsal
muscles.note: Its steady tone holds the lower lid down slightly.

muscles.name: Orbitalis
muscles.note: Vestigial in humans; may push the eye slightly forward.

muscles.name: Arrector pili
muscles.note: Raises the hairs into goose bumps in cold, fear or a thrill; one per hair follicle.

muscles.name: Dartos
muscles.note: Wrinkles and tightens the scrotal skin in cold and relaxes it in warmth, adjusting testicular temperature through the day.

muscles.name: Corrugator cutis ani
muscles.note: Wrinkles the skin around the anus; no meaningful everyday job.

muscles.name: Trachealis
muscles.note: Keeps tone in the back wall of the windpipe and narrows it in a cough to speed the airflow.

muscles.name: Bronchoesophageus
muscles.note: Anchoring band between the esophagus and the left bronchus; no clear active role.

muscles.name: Pleuroesophageus
muscles.note: Anchoring band between the esophagus and the pleura; no clear active role.

muscles.name: Pyloric sphincter
muscles.note: Lets food out of the stomach a little at a time for hours after each meal, and closes against backflow from the gut.

muscles.name: Suspensory muscle of duodenum
muscles.note: Thought to widen the bend where the duodenum meets the jejunum, easing food along.

muscles.name: Sphincter of hepatopancreatic ampulla
muscles.note: Holds back bile and pancreatic juice between meals and relaxes after you eat to release them.

muscles.name: Sphincter of bile duct
muscles.note: Keeps the bile duct shut between meals so bile fills the gallbladder.

muscles.name: Sphincter of pancreatic duct
muscles.note: Keeps bile from backing up into the pancreatic duct.

muscles.name: Internal anal sphincter
muscles.note: Provides most of the resting clench that keeps the anus closed day and night; relaxes briefly as the rectum fills so its contents can be sensed.

muscles.name: Rectococcygeus
muscles.note: Anchors the rectum to the tailbone; thought to steady it during a bowel movement.

muscles.name: Rectourethralis
muscles.note: Male; a band tying the rectum to the urethra, important in surgery but with no clear active role.

muscles.name: Detrusor
muscles.note: Relaxes as the bladder fills, then squeezes it empty each time you urinate, typically four to eight times a day.

muscles.name: Trigone muscle
muscles.note: Keeps the ureter openings closed against backflow, especially while you urinate.

muscles.name: Internal urethral sphincter
muscles.note: Keeps the bladder neck closed around the clock; in males it also shuts during ejaculation.

muscles.name: Pubovesicalis
muscles.note: Thought to help open the bladder neck when you urinate.

muscles.name: Rectovesicalis
muscles.note: A band of smooth muscle between the bladder and rectum; no clear active role.

muscles.name: Myocardium
muscles.note: Contracts about 100,000 times a day without rest, and harder whenever you climb stairs or hurry.

muscles.name: Pectinate muscles
muscles.note: Ridges of the atrial walls that contract with every beat.

muscles.name: Papillary muscles of right ventricle
muscles.note: Tighten the cords of the tricuspid valve with every beat so the valve cannot flip back.

muscles.name: Papillary muscles of left ventricle
muscles.note: Tighten the cords of the mitral valve with every beat.

muscles.name: Trabeculae carneae
muscles.note: Muscle ridges of the ventricle walls that contract with every beat; the moderator band carries the heartbeat signal across the right ventricle.
